objective.text: Ignore the server-selected current model in uniqueness validation without trusting a submitted ignore ID.

difficulty.rationale: Keep the excluded uniqueness row tied to the authorized update target.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: An authorized update targets account 7. The caller submits account_id=9 and an email already owned by account 9. The rule ignores $request->input("account_id"), so validation passes incorrectly. Which replacement excludes only the actual record being updated?

options.text: Ignore both the route account ID and the submitted account_id.
options.rationale: Excluding the unrelated row 9 would preserve the very bypass that must be prevented.
options.misconception: Excluding the unrelated row 9 would preserve the very bypass that must be prevented.

options.text: Use Rule::unique("accounts", "email")->ignore($account), where $account is the server-resolved account 7.
options.rationale: The trusted model supplies the real update identity, so the conflicting row 9 remains part of the uniqueness check.

options.text: Remove the unique rule whenever the request contains account_id.
options.rationale: Presence of an attacker-controlled field cannot justify skipping the uniqueness requirement.
options.misconception: Presence of an attacker-controlled field cannot justify skipping the uniqueness requirement.

options.text: Cast the submitted account_id to int and keep using it in ignore().
options.rationale: Type conversion does not establish that the submitted ID is the authorized update target.
options.misconception: Type conversion does not establish that the submitted ID is the authorized update target.
